German Far-Right Party Wins Saxony-Anhalt Election, Sparking Concern

The Alternative for Germany (AfD) party, led by Ulrich Siegmund, has achieved a significant victory in the Saxony-Anhalt election. Chancellor Friedrich Merz stated he was "deeply shocked" by the result, describing it as a shake-up for mainstream politicians in Europe. The win has raised concerns about potential risks to Germany's economic recovery and the possibility of further political fragmentation in Berlin, which could delay necessary reforms. Supporters of the AfD expressed a renewed sense of unity following the victory.
